feature1.prompt: Provide a way for model formsets to disallow new object creation. Model formsets don't provide a way to create an "edit only" view of objects. Users have resorted to using extra=0 to try to enforce an edit-only mode, but extra is only meant to control the number of extra forms displayed and is not reliable for this purpose. The solution must ensure that when operating in edit-only mode, only existing objects are updated and any data for new objects is ignored.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves updating the backend logic of Django formsets. Developers should modify the save method in django/forms/models.py so that if the edit_only flag is True, new objects are not created. In addition, the modelformset_factory and inlineformset_factory functions should be extended to accept an edit_only parameter and pass it properly to the resulting formset. This change should prevent new object creation when the mode is enabled.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/forms/models.py. Focus on the save method where both existing and new objects are saved. Update modelformset_factory (around lines 875-900) and inlineformset_factory (around lines 1076-1115) to include the new edit_only parameter and assign it to the FormSet.

feature2.prompt: Provide a way for model formsets to disallow new object creation by ensuring an effective edit-only mode. Model formsets currently allow the creation of new objects because there is no strict mechanism to enforce an edit-only view, and using extra=0 is an unreliable workaround. The fix should guarantee that when edit-only mode is enabled, any data submitted for new objects is ignored and only modifications to existing objects are applied. This functionality will improve the integrity of object updates in scenarios where only editing is intended.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on adding tests to verify that the edit-only mode works as expected. Developers should update the tests in tests/model_formsets/tests.py to add new test cases that simulate submitting extra data and confirm that no new objects are created. Key tests to implement include checks for standard formsets, inline formsets, and cases where objects outside the current queryset are submitted. Ensure that these tests capture the failure condition before the fix and the success condition after the fix.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/model_formsets/tests.py. Add new functions such as test_edit_only, test_edit_only_inlineformset_factory, and test_edit_only_object_outside_of_queryset to simulate form submissions in edit-only mode and verify that only existing objects are updated.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with django/forms/models.py for the core logic and tests/model_formsets/tests.py for verification. The edit_only flag and its propagation through formset factories are central shared components.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 implements the backend changes to enable an edit-only mode, while Feature2 provides thorough testing to validate that these changes work correctly. The integration will require ensuring that the interface exposed by the backend (the edit_only flag) is properly exercised and validated by the tests.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 should coordinate over the design and propagation of the edit_only parameter, the expected behavior in various formset scenarios, and the structure of the tests. Regular communication is essential to align the core logic changes with the test expectations and to resolve any discrepancies during integration.
